posts.cooked:
I would just like to throw into the conversation that for attempting to objectively analyze a deck, the majority of the post relates his deck to other heroes.  Not only that, but multiple "better" heroes to boot.  His extra play mechanic is likened to Tachyon, his search mechanic is likened to Wraith, his damage boost mechanic is likened to Legacy, etc.  Instead of focusin on the combos specific to CRs deck, the analysis is instead focused on how parts of that deck compare with other decks.  This doesn't seem all that objective.  Sure, I'll grant make a few comparisons to get a point accross.  But this isn't that.  This is using "better" decks to point out flaws in a deck, and as soon as the term better is thrown around without a solid definition of what better is, we dive right back into the realm of subjectivity.

Now, I'm no super player, and I don't have the deck-building, strategic-card-game-playing background as I'm assuming a lot of players on this forum (I'm typically a tabletop/sRPG gamer, with the exception of a brief stint into MTG), but just to echo what the other posters have said, each deck has its own time to shine.  If I know that I need to hit the primary villain target as hard and fast as I can, CR is one of the best options in my book.  As it has been discussed before, even against a villain target other than his nemesis, CR can get to 20 or so points of damage per turn, by turn two, without using HH or being boosted from the outside.  Not only that, but his "inflexible" damage boosting means that I know my allies are going to be hitting harder against the target I need them to hit harder against.  Instead of inflexible, its pinpoint shooting.

This topic, I know, will never come to a resolution with both sides agreeing.  There are just some points that neither side is willing to change their view on.  I will grant that, in comparison to other decks that allow extra card plays, with the exception of Expatriette, he seems to have limited card draws.  But for what his deck is supposed to do, his card draws are plenty, most of them deal damage while also getting a card draw, and are in the deck for a second purpose.  Compared to the three combined decks of Tachyon, Legacy, and Wraith, yes, he is vastly weaker.  But that wouldn't be a very objective, nor a very fair, conclusion to draw.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Chrono is based around his bounties.  10 cards pull them from his deck.

You want card draw, pull kill on sight, then recycle it with his 6 cards that pull bounties from the trash.

16 cards of his deck are based on using and reusing Bounties.  That's 40% of his deck.

With kill on sight you fuel your hand and hat.

With The Whole Gang you have a reverse Final Dive.

With No Executions you have a very powrful situational card.

With The Ultimate Target you gain extra powers and bonus damage.

With By any Means you gain damage, and so does your team.

Bounty Board is a phenomenal way to fuel your hat.  Use you on destruct bounties, then pull them back out and reuse them.

Bounty Board and Kill on sight are enough to fuel Jim's Hat for an entire game, there's no value to having cards in your hand at the end of the game if you could have played them.

Who else can let C-R put HaH out and survive, besides Legacy?

The Naturalist, Tachyon, Mr. Fixer, Haka, Wraith, The Sentinels, Sky-Scraper, The Scholar, Fanatic, Unity, Vis+Ra, Setback.

Is that enough?  We can add Bloogo if you want.

There's also plenty of rounds you can pay attention and find out you aren't likely to get hit to play it, or just play it and understand that you can hit them more times than they can hit you, and burn them down faster.

With Grand Warlord Voss and Chrono I have wiped a Forced Deployment of 5 minions including a Guard with an Ultimate Target and other bounties, Hunter and Hunted and Danny-Boy.  Not one of the minions even acted.

That's with no outside support.  No other deck can do that.  So yeah, if they had dealt damage Chrono was screwed.  But they didn't, because he killed them all first.

The strength of Hunter and Hunted is the win condition of almost all of the villains.

Chrono Ranger doesn't need to live long if the villain lives even shorter.  When you hit the point where you can pull that off that's when you play H&H.  Recognizing that point in the match is the key to using it well.

posts.cooked:
I was going to try an engage in a sensible debate, and hopefully I still can, because I honestly love Chrono-Ranger and how he plays, despite the fact I don't use many of his cards. Hope you forgive some ramblings, I tend to be long winded.

 

First a side note about tone, using phrases like "I am showing how to objectively analyze decks." is slightly hostile, as it assumes that the reader cannot objectively analyze for themselves. It probably wasn't your intention, but small things like this really change how you are perceived on the internet and make debates much harder. I admit that phrase almost got me to stop reading before you even began.

 

Secondly, about the above quotes involving Jim's Hat. While it may seem internally consistent to someone who is writing the piece, stating something not true (such as all Jim's equipments give only an additional damage power) then later saying that there is an equipment that is worthless that does not give a power does not look consisten to an outsider, it looks as though the writer either forgot or did not know about the fact when they began writing. I used to get called to task on things like that all the time, so I understand, but it is an important thing to remeber that the audience will have an imperfect understanding of your intended flow.

 

On to some counterpoints:

1) My first counter is perhaps the biggest, and the most glaring lack in your argument. There are 24 cards in CR's deck that have the effect "deal 1 target 1 projectile damage". The only cards that do not have this effect are Hunter and Hunted, his equipment cards, and his bounties. This means 60% of his deck is a damaging one-shot. This is what makes the Hat the first card I go for unless I absolutely need a weapon. With Jim's hat you are essentially capable of using his base power 3 times a turn, more if you get  Eye on the Prize. This is also why increasing CR's damage is such a huge boost. He has so many possible instances of damage that the effect is multiplied many times over. As an example: Displaced Armory, put Jim's Hat into play, deal 1 damage, Eye on the Prize, deal 1 damage, draw and play Terrible teck strike, deal 2 damage followed by 1 damage, use base power for one damage. That's playing 4 cards and dealing 5 damage in one turn with no outside assistance. Add in a +1 or 2 from the proper bounties and things quickly spiral. These riders also mean that CR pretty much never has a dead card in his hand, as he can always just play it for damage.

 

2) You specifically called out Temporal Grenades as not being a terribly great card, and I'd like to counter. Compare it to Tachyon's Blinding Speed. Blinding speed destroys exactly one ongoing or environment target as well, and is a burst which means it is a possible damage further down the line. That is not guarenteed in any way though, just possible. Also, it cannot work if Tachyon cannot play cards because it is a one-shot and if it is played accidentally it is wasted. Grenades is guarenteed automatic damage, and it can sit on the field until you want to use it, accidental plays don't matter. Also Displaced Armory allows you to pull from the trash, meaning it is possible to bring back the grenades if you need them again. They are also the only equipment that CR has multiple copies of, only two copies but still.

 

3) Just doing My Job. I understand where it is possible to see this card as a net loss for the team, however, I disagree for two points. First, as mentioned above, this card has the rider "Deal 1 target 1 projectile damage". Even if you or your team use it for nothing else, that is helpful. Secondly, it is incredibly rare for someone to not have a card they are willing to discard. Fanatic's End of Days when you are already set up, AZ's sub-zero atmosphere (I never really use that card) Ra's flesh of the Sun God or Wrathful Gaze, Almost any of Tachyon's burst cards. The benefit of drawing does go entirely to CR, but he gets a lot of damage mileage out of every card he plays so in the goal of dropping the villain it can be a very benficial tradeoff. It is also completely optional, if the heroes don't want to lose any of the cards, they don't have to.

 

4) Hunter and Hunted. You seem a little obsessive about this card in CR's deck, and I get it becuase it is his big, final move card. First of all, yes, it is a suicide run. I would never keep this card out for more than 2 turns unless I needed to, and I'm willing to die in the next few rounds. That or the team is curb-stomping the villain. However, there is a reason it is a suicide run card, the benefit of playing it is enormous. Let's put it in the ideal, ultimate set up that will never happen. 6 bounties out, the two damage buffs on the main villain, Compound bow (easily Jim's most powerful weapon), the Hat. Play HaH all your damage is increased by +6, this means against the main target you hit at a +8. PLay any one-shot, deal 9 damage to the villain, then use the Bow for another 18 damage. That's 27 damage, no penalty. Same as Fanatic using Wrathful Retribution when she is at 3 hp, minus the card draw. Villain hits you, you take an additional six damage, but if you planned for it you are likely still standing, Ultimate target allows you to use a power, Bow for 18 damage. Total damage is now 45, this is a near fully charged omnicannon, or a big savage mana powered up with a Haka of battle. Your only cost so far was +6 damage to yourself. Next turn, play two cards, deal 18 damage, use bow, 18 damage. That's an additional 36 damage for a grand total of 81 damage in 2 rounds. Now I understand, this is a set-up that will not happen, many things could go wrong and mess this up, but HaH is suicide because it is a big damage buff to CR, a guy who gets the absolute most mileage from damage buffs. He only needs for it to last 1 round to make the most of it. However, the truth about HaH is the same truth about any heroes Final Move, big damage card. It is completely unneccessary for CR to get the job done, he doesn't need it to be effective.

 

I think that sums up my major points.

No, you created an extremely hypothetical situation in which you were somehow able to get 8 cards to stay in play, somehow wind up with the correct HP to force the Villain to attack C-R instead of another hero target, and conveniently not get hit by any environment or new villain draws. Anything is possible, but anything is not probable, and if it is not probable, you do not rely on it… or cite it as a fundamental strength.

For the perfect mashed potato there are two key steps, simple yet effective changes that you can make to your usual recipe and which will unlock a step change in flavour and texture experience.

The first is to follow a more refined cooking method. Potatoes are full of starch, which reacts differently depending on the way it is heated. Rapid boiling can cause the starches to become sticky, resulting in a gloopy and lumpy final texture. By heating the potato from cold to a gentle simmer, then removing them and rapidly cooling down in cold water, you will break up the starch strands. You can then return the potato to a full boil until cooked through and the resultant texture will be much smoother and fluffier.

The second tip will help you to lock in an incredible amount of lost flavour and is even more simple to follow. Simply reserve the washed peeled skins and add to a saucepan of warm milk. Allow the skins to infuse the milk on a low heat for as long as possible and use the drained potato flavoured milk in your finished dish in place of plain milk. As most of the flavour is in the skin of the potato this will transform your humble spuds from side dish to centrepiece!

If you want to go one step further you can also spruce up further with a sprinkling of lime zest, an ideal flavour pairing with potato.
